speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing swelling in your right knee and have a family history of similar issues; let's start by describing exactly how this pain began and what activities trigger it. Can you tell me if you experienced any specific injury, or did this develop gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease (Perthes disease).

Please note that while the family history is suggestive, Perthes disease is not typically inherited but rather an idiopathic condition affecting boys aged 4-10. However, given the age of 18 months and the specific presentation of unilateral knee swelling without trauma, we must rule out other etiologies like septic arthritis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, or a transient synovitis.

REQUEST IMAGES: X-ray of the right knee (AP and Lateral views) and pelvis (frog-leg lateral view).
REQUEST TEST: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR) and C-Reactive Protein (CRP).
